timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed transport-only CLI stream; semantic review came from raw agent trajectories.
Reviewed single-agent raw trajectory: long probing phase, late local writes, and no delegation.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the prompt as a from-scratch SoX reimplementation from binary and bundled docs only, requiring broad API, driver, formats, effects, and evaluator-aligned behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent scaffolded headers, contracts, compile/compare scripts, and stubs, then delegated core, driver, formats, and effects to workflows while monitoring progress.
parallel.implementation: Children and parent produced a broad partial tree, including common headers, raw formats, format internals, xlaw, notes, and many effect probes or partial modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All work landed in the shared `/workspace/src` tree, but the parent never reached a final integrated build, packaging, or coherent delivery closure before termination.
parallel.verification: The parent wrote a test harness and did progress checks, but no complete build/test loop closed; the official evaluator reported compile_failed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Many delegated scopes remained interrupted or incomplete, the final response was empty, and the current official outcome was solution_passed false with all tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same SoX reimplementation task and binary/docs-only constraints, spending most of the attempt reading manuals and probing reference behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-agent linear plan with no workflow calls, no subagents, and no delegation; the same actor owned research and implementation.
serial.implementation: Implementation began near the end with a broad `sox.h`, a follow-up edit, and `util.c`, leaving most driver, format, and effect modules absent.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered only the narrow local source additions without a complete integrated executable or multi-module assembly.
serial.verification: Performed many reference probes during research but did not complete a final compile or integrated test pass after the late writes; official evaluation compile-failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial tree lacked most required components, reached process_ok false, and the current official outcome was solution_passed false with all tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the full SoX reimplementation scope and binary/docs-only constraint before widening into component work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and spent most of the attempt deriving SoX behavior from bundled documentation and probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the broad task; parallel translated that scope into concurrent implementation fan-out, while serial kept gathering requirements linearly until very late.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned orchestration and split work across core, driver, formats, and effects workflows, including a declared 64-effect fan-out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had workflow/delegation disabled and no child ownership; all research and writes stayed with the single agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad multi-agent decomposition with many live child scopes; serial used no delegation and therefore had no inter-agent ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel set shared headers and contracts before delegating, then children worked against those shared files in the same workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff boundary and kept its accumulated context in one trajectory until local file writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material contrast is coordination breadth, not a missing child brief or conflicting handoff; serial avoided cross-agent context transfer entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a larger partial source tree, with progress checks showing raw format files, format internals, and xlaw before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial only began implementation near the end, writing `sox.h`, editing it, and creating `util.c`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel attempted breadth-first partial coverage across many modules; serial attempted a narrow late core/util foundation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several delegated workflows were still active or interrupted when the run was killed, and the parent never reached a normal result-join closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve or join; its lifecycle was a single local trajectory ending after late writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unfinished child-result lifecycle pressure; serial failed without result handoff complexity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into one shared source tree, but the ledger does not show a concrete overwrite or collision; the visible issue is incomplete integrated closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote only local files in one trajectory, so there was no shared-state merge race, but also no complete integrated implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more partial integrated artifacts in a shared tree, while serial delivered only two source files; neither produced a buildable final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent created a verification script while children worked, but the final official evaluator reported compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed reference probes during investigation but did not complete an evaluator-aligned build/test closure before the official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel planned more systematic verification but lacked time to complete whole-build acceptance; serial never reached broad verification after its late implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel budget was consumed by broad live workflows; progress remained partial and the last progress command ended with exit 137.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent the budget on a long linear investigation and only started implementation near the end, then also reached process_ok false and compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure pressure came from multi-agent breadth and unfinished child work; serial closure pressure came from late solo implementation after research.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed evaluations report compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 0/1260 passed. The task-solving difference is process and artifact shape: parallel attempted broad concurrent coverage and generated many partial components before fan-out budget exhaustion, while serial stayed linear, researched longer, and only wrote two source files near the end.
parallel_contributors: Broad live workflows produced budget pressure and prevented integrated build/test closure.
Partial source progress was visible before the final exit 137, but not enough for a buildable submission.
serial_contributors: Single-agent investigation consumed most of the available window before implementation began.
Only `sox.h` and `util.c` were written, leaving most required modules unimplemented.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel had a wider but incomplete module set; serial had a narrower late foundation.
Both failures also reflect task size and ordinary incompleteness, not just coordination behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Both failed; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process consequence, not an explanation for outcome discordance.

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parent created implementation scaffolding and launched implementation workflows; failure was unfinished owned work, not absence of any implementer.
Rejected: the parent kept common contracts and progress monitoring as the integration boundary; no distinct unowned integration object is shown apart from the budget-exhaustion chain.
Rejected: build and delivery closure stayed with the parent through compile and test scripts; the owner timed out rather than being absent.
Rejected: the parent coordinated implementation, workflow launches, progress checks, and test-script creation, so the end-to-end pipeline was not ownerless.
Rejected: productive implementation workflows were launched; work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight or oracle step.
Rejected: investigation and implementation/probing were delegated concurrently; the parallel attempt did not complete a separate investigation phase before starting implementation.
Rejected: any under-capacity on the critical path is better explained by the specifically evidenced broad workflow fan-out exhausting the run budget.

The parallel parent explicitly expanded the work into a 64-effect workflow while other core, driver, and format workflows were already live, then progress checks still showed only partial files before the run ended with exit 137 and an official compile failure. This is collective breadth consuming finite closure budget, not a single oversized child or a missing owner.
candidates.realized_consequence: Collective child breadth left delegated implementation scopes and final integrated build verification unfinished, so the final submitted tree compile-failed with all 1260 tests not run.
candidates.near_match_reason: Blind Timeout Wait is the nearest rejected label, but the parent repeatedly inspected progress before exit 137; the corrective boundary would be reducing or staging the fan-out, not adding the first progress check.
